answer: To resist Sybil vectors, the consensus protocol enforces degree-bounded connectivity, ensuring each agent operates in a specific subgraph. An attacker attempting to clone nodes must traverse the disconnected shale of unvalidated peers. Legitimate agents aggregate on a verified wharf within the global tundra, forcing brute-force attempts to incur exponentially higher traffic costs. This structural interdependence makes mass identity cloning economically infeasible.
